newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche says sales accelerated in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Roche says sales accelerated in Q2.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said sales picked up speed in the second quarter, helping to push first-half turnover up 20 percent in terms of Swiss francs to 9.3 billion francs.
"Particularly in the pharmaceuticals and diagnostics division, sales advanced faster than during the first quarter," it said in a statement.

Roche announced the acquisition of Corange in the second quarter, making it a market leader in diagnostics and strengthening its share in major pharmaceutiucal markets. The deal must still be approved by anti-trust authorities.
Its acquisition of Tastemaker was approved on March 31, making it the world's largest supplier of flavours as well.
Roche gave these descriptions of sales by division:
PHARMACEUTICALS:

Sales rose 20 percent in Swiss francs and six percent in local currencies. The growth rate increased despite generic competition following expiry of patent protection for Rivotril/Klonopin brand. Top-selling prescription drugs Rocephin, Roaccutane/Accutane, Dormicum/Versed, Neupogen and Ticlid brands continued to show double-digit growth. Sales of AIDS drug Invirase and CellCept, used in transplan t medicine, more than doubled compared with the first half of 1996. Double-digit local currency sales increases boosted market share in Germany, Italy and Spain. "In the United States the drop in Rivotril/Klonopin sales resulting from generic competition was offset by rising sales for other products. Sales growth remained good in Latin America and Asia," it said.

Roche said regulatory review of its Xenical anti-obesity drug and Tasmar, for treating Parkinson's Disease, was proceeding on schedule in all major markets. It said the global sales force had been substantially expanded once again in preparation for the product launches.
"Half-year sales for the OTC (non-prescription) business were also up by two figures," it said.
VITAMINS AND FINE CHEMICALS
Sales rose 16 percent in Swiss francs and three percent in local currencies.

"Despite sustained pressure on prices, the vitamins and fine chemicals division recorded increased sales, expanding its market share for biotin and vitamins C, B1, B6 and B2 on strong volume growth," it said. Substantial volume growth was reported for vitamins A and E, dexpanthenol and astaxanthin.
"Demand in Europe and North America was restrained. Above-average growth rates were achieved in China and in most Latin American and Southeast Asia markets."
DIAGNOSTICS:
Sales up 27 percent in Swiss francs, 15 percent in local currencies

Division sales growth was well ahead of the market average, with all business segments contributing to the good result. The drug monitoring and immunochemistry business posted double-digit growth. Demand was strong for all analytical systems introduced over the past two years. Sales of products based on polymerase chain reaction technology nearly doubled.
FRAGRANCES AND FLAVOURS
Sales up 25 percent in Swiss francs, 12 percent local

"Sales were up in the fragrances segment, helped by major new accounts and by strong demand in the Asia-Pacific region and North America. Increased flavour sales in Europe and Asia contributed to the division's good half-year results."
It said the due diligence review concerning its acquisition of Corange, the holding company for Boehringer Mannheim and DePuy, was proceeding on schedule.
"It is expected to be several more months before the authorities approve the transaction," it said, adding it would use this time to plan the integration of new members in the group.
Roche said it would publish a detailed half-year report in mid-August.
